patients.summary: Travel agent and daily smoker on a combined estrogen pill who joins the practice in 2023 with migraine, mild depression and irregular menses. Three pulmonary emboli after long flights (April 2025, October 2025, April 2026); the pill is stopped only after the third, and she is now on indefinite apixaban.

documents.title: New patient intake call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller wants to move her primary care here; her old office has had a hard time getting her in around her work travel. Booked a new-patient appointment for 8/22 at 2:40 pm. Gave her the release form so we can get her old office's chart. Insurance card photo uploaded through the portal while on the line.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
38 yo woman transferring care. Books international trips for a living, mostly from a desk, but she is on a long-haul flight several times a year for work.

Headaches: migraines since her early twenties, a few a month, throbbing and one-sided with nausea and light sensitivity. No visual or sensory warning before them, no weakness. Dark room and sleep take care of most; she has never wanted a prescription for them.

Mood: a depressive episode about two years ago, mild, worked through it on her own and with friends. Never took medication, never saw a therapist. Some low days still. PHQ-9 today 7. No thoughts of self-harm.

Gyn: cycles have been irregular for years; started a combined pill around 2017 for that and it keeps her regular. Takes it daily, no missed packs to speak of. Not trying to conceive.

Tobacco: a pack a day, has smoked since about 19, so roughly 20 pack-years. Has tried cold turkey twice. Not interested in patches or pills right now. Alcohol a drink or two a month. No drugs.

No surgeries. No medication allergies.
Family: mother had a DVT at 45. Father has high blood pressure. An uncle on her father's side had a blood clot in the lung.

Meds: ethinyl estradiol 0.035 / norgestimate 0.25, one daily.

Exam: well, pleasant. Vitals as recorded. HEENT unremarkable, neck supple without thyroid enlargement. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Legs without swelling. Neuro nonfocal. Affect a little flat but appropriate.

A/P:
1. Migraine without aura, episodic. Lifestyle triggers reviewed. Return if frequency changes.
2. Mild depression, single episode, residual low mood. Watchful; she would rather not start anything. Rescreen next visit.
3. Irregular menses on combined pill. Refills here going forward.
4. Cigarette dependence. Strongly encouraged quitting; she knows where to find us when ready.
5. Health maintenance: CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH, one-time HIV and hep C screens today. Requesting her old office's records for her last Pap.
Follow up in about 6 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Morgan, all of the blood work from Tuesday looks fine: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, thyroid and cholesterol are normal, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to do there. Good meeting you.

reports.text: Specimen adequate for evaluation; transformation zone component present. Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV not detected.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Faxed chart from her previous primary care office, 41 pages, scanned. Includes visit notes 2017 to 2023, a Pap with HPV co-test from May 2021 (negative for lesion, HPV not detected), and pill prescriptions going back to 2017. Routed to PCP for review.

PCP addendum: reviewed. Nothing new beyond what she told us. Next cervical screening due 2026.

documents.title: Immunization visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here before work for her seasonal shots. Feeling well, no fever. Influenza vaccine in the left deltoid and the updated COVID vaccine in the right deltoid. Lot numbers in the immunization record. Observed afterward, no reaction. VIS sheets given.

documents.title: Refill request: oral contraceptive
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Pharmacy e-request for ethinyl estradiol/norgestimate, 3 packs with 3 refills. Last seen 8/2023. Pended for PCP.

PCP: approved, 3 packs x 3 refills.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Six-month check. Winter has been busy at work with people booking spring trips; she has been in the office more than usual.

Mood about the same, steady, sleeping okay. PHQ-9 6. Declines counseling referral again, though she took the list of local therapists.
Headaches: two or three a month, same pattern as before, no new features, nothing that wakes her.
Cycles regular on the pill.
Still at about a pack a day. We talked through what quitting could look like; she wants to try cutting back on her own first.

Vitals as recorded. Looks well. Heart and lungs normal.

Plan: continue current pill. Recheck mood at the physical in the fall. Book the physical before she leaves the office.

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body:
So sorry about yesterday, I was stuck at the airport after a delayed connection and completely forgot to call. Everything is fine on my end. Can we just roll it into my physical in September?

Front desk reply 6/13: no problem, you're set for 9/24 at 10:00.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, just turned 40.

Interval: no illnesses, no ED visits. Headaches unchanged at a couple a month. Mood a bit lower this summer with long hours; PHQ-9 8, mild range. No self-harm thoughts. She still prefers no medication and no therapy right now; we agreed to keep an eye on it and she will message if it slides.
Cycles regular on the pill. LMP two weeks ago.
Smoking about a pack a day, the cutting-back plan did not stick. Again offered help when she wants it.
Travel: roughly six long-haul trips this year for work.

Meds: ethinyl estradiol 0.035 / norgestimate 0.25 daily. No medication allergies.

Exam: well-appearing. Vitals as recorded. Eyes, ears, throat normal. No thyroid enlargement or nodes. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Breasts without masses, skin changes or nipple discharge, no axillary nodes. Abdomen soft, nontender. No leg swelling. Skin without suspicious lesions.

A/P:
- Health maintenance: CBC, CMP and lipids today. Tdap today (none on record). Screening mammogram ordered. Pap due 2026. Flu and COVID later this fall when the season's supply comes in.
- Mild depression: watchful, rescreen at each visit.
- Migraine: no change.
- Tobacco: counseled.
RTC one year, or sooner as needed.

reports.text: Bilateral digital screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. No prior studies for comparison. The breasts are scattered areas of fibroglandular density. No suspicious mass, architectural distortion or suspicious calcifications in either breast.
reports.conclusion: BI-RADS 1: negative. Routine annual screening recommended.

documents.title: Mammogram result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your mammogram came back normal, no findings. We'll plan to repeat it next year.

documents.title: Immunization visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Seasonal flu and 2024-25 COVID vaccines given, one in each arm. Afebrile, no complaints. Tolerated without issue and left after the observation period.
